svg.title: The concentration gap: ivermectin far, mebendazole closer
svg.desc: Log-scale comparison of drug concentrations. Ivermectin: the 28-cell-line lab study used 5 micromolar; the Stromectol label’s mean peak blood level after a 12 mg dose is 46.6 ng/mL, about 0.053 micromolar, 94 times lower. If levels rise in proportion to dose, as the label says, a 25 mg capsule would reach about 0.11 micromolar (45 times lower) and 120 mg about 0.53 micromolar (9 times lower). Mebendazole: lab IC50s in a glioma cell panel were 0.11 to 0.31 micromolar; the Emverm label says blood levels stay at or below 0.03 mcg/mL (0.10 micromolar) at 100 mg twice daily; a trial dosing up to 4 g a day targeted 300 ng/mL (1.0 micromolar) and 5 of 11 patients reached it.

text.font-family: Inter, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Ivermectin’s lab doses are far above human blood levels

svg.text: Micromolar (µM), log scale. Mebendazole’s gap is much smaller, but levels vary a lot from person to person
